en: The Sūtra on the Ritual Manual for the Amoghapāśa Dhāraṇī Spoken by the Buddha, Scroll One;
also titled: The Secret Mantra of the Teaching of Amoghapāśa.
Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Amoghavajra of Siṃhala Island, by Imperial Decree.
Thus have I heard.
At one time the Buddha was dwelling among the Śuddhāvāsa devas,
together with a great assembly of devas and the Śuddhāvāsa deva kings.
The celestial king Īśvara, the celestial king Maheśvara,
the celestial king Mahābrahmā, the celestial king Śakra,
and the hosts of devas sat upon lion thrones of precious lotuses and preached the sublime Dharma.
Surpassing all like the light of the sun illuminating everything,
at that time the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara rose from his seat with joy and exultation.
Baring his right shoulder, he joined his palms in reverence;
having prostrated at the Buddha’s feet and adjusted his robes,
he knelt with hands folded before him and addressed the Buddha, saying:
World-Honored One,
I possess a dhāraṇī called the King of Hearts of the Amoghapāśa Dhāraṇī Mantra Samaya Dharma.
In the past, ninety-one kalpas ago,
during the very last of those kalpas, a Buddha appeared in the world,
named Lokeśvararāja Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, Perfect in Knowledge and Conduct, Sugata, Knower of the World, Unsurpassed One, Tamer of Men, Teacher of Gods and Humans, Bhagavān.
Out of compassion for me, that Buddha, the World-Honored One,
bestowed this dhāraṇī mantra, the gateway to all dharmas.
That buddha-world is named Superior Contemplation Wisdom.
"World-Honored One, from that time forth,
I have constantly upheld this dharani-mantra and all its teachings of the Dharma,
guiding and transforming immeasurable hundreds of thousands of sentient beings."
These were the celestial kings of the Śuddhāvāsa heaven,
the celestial king Īśvara, the celestial king Maheśvara, the celestial king Mahābrahmā,
and the celestial king Śakra; all these celestial kings, together with their respective retinues.
They shall honor, make offerings to, respect, and praise them,
causing all to abide in *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*,
and adorning them all with the wisdom that is free from the net of doubt.
"Bhagavān, when I first attained this dharma of dhāraṇī,
I realized hundreds of thousands of non-empty, unerring wisdoms,
and the gateways of the samādhi 'Adorned Head' all manifested before me."
By the power of this mantra, the World-Honored One directly beheld the assemblies of all the Buddha-Tathāgatas in the various, immeasurable, and innumerable lands throughout the ten directions.
They all made offerings and listened to the profound Dharma;
through successive teaching and transformation,
they brought immeasurable sentient beings to set out toward unsurpassed bodhi.
Therefore, the wise should receive and uphold it.
World-Honored One, wherever this sutra is practiced,
one should know that in that place there are immeasurable hundreds of thousands of kings of the Śuddhāvāsa heavens and King Īśvara.
The Great Brahmā Heavenly King, Śakra Devendra,
and all twelve million hundred thousand heavenly kings, together with their retinues,
constantly protect, revere, and surround them.
World-Honored One, in whatever place this sutra may be found, should there be those who,
according to the Dharma, transcribe it with purity,
read, recite, uphold, and praise it;
One should know that such a place is a *caitya* containing the entire bodies of all Buddhas.
World-Honored One, if any sentient beings are able to even briefly recite, hear, or listen [to it], [they shall attain great merit].
Those who propagate this mantra-samaya of the Heart-King Dhāraṇī of Amoghapāśa should know that such persons shall personally approach,
revere, and make offerings to immeasurable koṭis, nayutas, hundreds of thousands of Buddhas.
They have planted all manner of roots of goodness in the presence of all Buddhas. Why is this?
Because this Dharma is the precious accumulation of the bodhi of all Buddhas.
Bhagavān, if there are sentient beings who commit extremely evil deeds—
slandering all Buddhas, bodhisattvas, pratyekabuddhas, and śrāvakas,
as well as slandering the True Dharma by claiming that no goodness exists— [how can they be purified?]
Furthermore, those who destroy Buddhas, Bodhisattvas, Pratyekabuddhas, or Śrāvakas,
or who slander images, stupas, temples, sutras, śāstras,
and the teachings, should fall into the Avīci Hell.
For incalculable kalpas, they undergo the sufferings of the Avīci hell;
even though the Buddhas, Bodhisattvas, Pratyekabuddhas,
and Śrāvakas possess supernatural powers, they cannot save them.
"Blessed One, when such sentient beings as these are able to give rise to a mind of remorse, bathe themselves until they are clean,
anoint their bodies with fragrances, and put on fresh, pure garments."
In accordance with the Dharma, one should sincerely repent before the Buddha for the grave offenses committed in past and present lives, vowing never to commit them again,
and maintain the precepts of fasting while purifying the mind.
Having refrained from all discourse for seven days and seven nights,
one who recites this dhāraṇī mantra one hundred and eight times daily before the Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara of Amoghapāśa—
It should be known that all the various offenses committed by such a person in previous lives— the ten evil deeds, the five heinous crimes, and the four grave transgressions—
will be extinguished without remainder,
and they shall not fall into hell.
Except for those who have committed the five heinous crimes and receive retribution lightly in the present life, how is this known?
It is as follows: for one day, two days, three days, four days, and even up to seven days.
Malaria, febrile diseases, or ailments of the eyes, ears, nose, tongue, gums, and teeth;
disorders of the head, back, both shoulders,
heart, abdomen, ribs, waist, thighs, both knees, hemorrhoids, dysentery, and cholera.
Painful itching and swelling of the hands and feet; white leprosy, wind-sores, and carbuncles;
scabies, ringworm, abscesses, and localized swellings;
boils, toxic swellings, jaundice, and hemorrhoids.
Suffering from diseases such as sores, blisters, itching, insanity, or malevolent sorcery;
being harassed and disturbed by ghosts and spirits;
or being subjected to various kinds of slander and insults by people.
Flogged and beaten, they endure various sufferings in a state of distress;
they encounter other misfortunes or inauspicious dreams.
World-Honored One, such people undergo these [retributions] lightly because of this.
It can eliminate the grave karmic retributions of all the intense sufferings of hell;
how much more so for sentient beings with pure faith who have committed minor offenses—
how could they not achieve accomplishment by receiving and upholding this dharani mantra?
If there are sentient beings whose bodies and minds are unsettled,
or who suffer from various calamities, fears, evil dreams, and inauspicious omens,
and who daily purify themselves, recite, uphold, burn incense, and make offerings [to this scripture], [they shall be freed from these afflictions].
Then they shall be extinguished.
World-Honored One, if there are good sons or good daughters who,
according to the Dharma, copy, receive and uphold, read, recite, and hear this teaching.
He teaches others to proclaim and praise it in accordance with the Dharma,
instructing them to copy, uphold, read, and recite it,
so as to cause all sentient beings— born from wombs, eggs, moisture, or by transformation— to widely [partake in it].
Those who hear this dharani mantra-samaya shall all attain liberation from all karmic obstacles.
Such sons and daughters of good family as these—
One should purify the mind by reflecting according to reality,
through the wisdom of non-apprehension and the wisdom of no fixed location.
The wisdom of no-self, no person, and no experiencer;
non-conceptual wisdom; and the wisdom of neither arising nor ceasing.
The wisdom of unimpeded movement;
the wisdom of non-action and non-attachment;
and the wisdom of equality.
Free from the five aggregates— form, sound, smell, taste, touch, and phenomena—
it is the diligence and wisdom that neither grasps nor rejects;
it is the skillful wisdom of suchness in its various aspects.
By controlling the mind and employing skillful means,
one should contemplate all Buddhas as if they were constantly present before one's eyes.
Before long, one shall attain the simultaneous manifestation of hundreds of thousands of all Buddhas of the ten directions.
They may stroke his head and offer praise as witnesses;
or he may see auspicious signs in dreams or upon waking;
or various Buddhas may manifest themselves as śramaṇas.
They shall bestow upon them the section on the Superior Bodhisattva Precepts,
causing all heavy sins accumulated over immeasurable hundreds of thousands of kalpas, as numerous as motes of dust, to be extinguished;
even to the point that they may transcribe this sutra according to the Dharma and install it within their own dwellings.
By offering incense and flowers according to one's heart, and by honoring and prostrating with respect,
the merit obtained shall likewise be such.
World-Honored One, this is merely a brief explanation of a small portion for now.
If there are sentient beings who, out of a mind of jealousy, flattery, or deception for the sake of surpassing others;
or out of fear, greed for wealth and profit, or frivolity based on dependence upon others;
should read, recite, listen to, or hear this dharani-mantra samaya.
In all cases, one obtains victory.
Furthermore, even if one hears [this teaching] with slander, contempt, and a lack of respect,
one still obtains victory.
World-Honored One, this present benefit is known only by those of great wisdom;
it is indeed the power of the majestic spiritual authority of the Tathāgata, Sovereign King of the World.
This is indeed the power of the great compassion of Avalokiteśvara,
which causes all sentient beings of evil disposition to plant immeasurable roots of goodness as soon as [his name] passes through their ears.
Why is that? World-Honored One,
it is as if there were a person who, with a foolish and evil mind,
went to a forest of camphor trees or other fragrant forests.
With a mind of deluded wisdom, he reviled the incense in various ways;
furthermore, with a heart of malice, he slandered it, saying, "This incense truly has no fragrance.
He took the incense, cut it into pieces, pounded it, and ground it into powder.
It may be drunk with water, eaten, or smeared upon the body.
This incense has no mind and does not say, "That person treats me with contempt.
For the nature of this incense is such that it can permeate everything.
Even things that lack fragrance become fragrant and aromatic.
World-Honored One, this Samaya of the Heart-King Dhāraṇī Mantra of the Amoghapāśa is likewise so.
If sentient beings deny cause and effect,
engage in various forms of slander seeking out faults and evils,
or act out of jealousy, deceit, and crookedness regarding wealth, food, and all manner of calamities;
By upholding, reciting, and making offerings [to this], one will,
through these causes and conditions, acquire great roots of goodness; thereafter,
in whatever place one is reborn after this life, [one shall...]
They constantly obtain the fragrance of ethical discipline, the fragrance of meditative concentration, the fragrance of wisdom, and the fragrance of liberation;
the fragrance of majestic power, fearlessness, and the accumulations of merit and knowledge;
and the fragrance of the mass of merit that is firm and indestructible, the essence of all enlightenment.
In whatever place they are born, they will be of noble lineage, perfected in a mass of merit,
adorned with the precepts and wisdom, and constantly able to benefit others.
World-Honored One, if there are good men or good women—
Those who uphold, recite, and chant this dhāraṇī should,
on the eighth, fourteenth, or fifteenth day of the waxing moon,
bathe themselves with purity, anoint their bodies with incense, and don clean garments.
Alternatively, one may abstain from food and cease all conversation;
then, sitting according to the ritual rules before the Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara of Amoghapāśa,
one should burn various kinds of famous incense.
Beholding the face of the Bodhisattva, one should recite this dhāraṇī seventy-seven times or one hundred and eight times.
World-Honored One, you should know that such a person shall attain twenty kinds of meritorious benefits and advantages in their present life.
What are the twenty?
First, the body is free from various ailments;
if illnesses arise due to past karma, they are swiftly eliminated.
Second, his skin is fine, soft, smooth, and exquisite.
Third, he is constantly gazed upon and cherished by all people without ever being weary of him.
Fourth, his six sense faculties are always settled, and wealth and treasures come to him spontaneously.
Fifth, one’s clothing, wealth, and treasures will not be plundered by bandits.
Sixth, all one’s wealth and treasures will not be consumed by fire or swept away by water.
Seventh, one will not be subjected to assault, murder, or the forcible seizure of wealth that leads to death by starvation.
Eighth, one shall not fall to one's death from a precipice.
Ninth, by empowering pure water and sprinkling it upon all fruits,
crops, and the like, one shall ward off evil winds, frost, hail, insects, and beasts.
Tenth, there shall be no disasters or calamities, and the crops will flourish.
Eleventh, they shall not die by being killed in military arrays or through strife and contention;
nor shall they die from having their vital essence sucked away or being harmed by the enmity of various evil spirits and ghosts of the world.
Twelfth, they are constantly praised and extolled by the multitude;
they cherish one another and do not meet with death during an evil age.
Thirteenth, if they see any non-Buddhists or wicked people, these naturally become harmonious and reconciled.
Fourteenth, one shall not be slandered or harmed by any evil persons;
should such things arise, they will quickly extinguish themselves.
Fifteenth, one will always be free from fear toward all humans and non-humans.
Sixteenth, one shall not die from being harmed by worldly curses, spells, incantations, or *ḍākinī* spirits.
Seventeenth, all evil latent tendencies (*anuśaya*) and afflictions (*kleśa*) will naturally be extinguished.
Eighteenth, one shall not suffer death through harm from fire, water, burning, drowning, blades, arrows, poisons, venomous insects, or calamities.
Nineteenth, all the devas shall constantly provide protection.
Twentieth: wherever one is born, one shall possess great loving-kindness, great compassion, great sympathetic joy, and great equanimity, as well as the four kinds of unhindered minds.
Furthermore, World-Honored One, there are eight other dharmas.
What are the eight? First, at the time of death,
the Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara manifests his own body in the form of a śramaṇa.
First, through skillful means they will be guided and led to the Buddha-fields.
Second, at the time of death, their bodies will experience no pain;
they will be free and at ease in going and staying, as if entering meditative concentration.
Third, at the time of death,
one’s eyes do not wander restlessly nor manifest the signs of a miserable death.
Fourth, at the time of death...
Fifth, at the time of death, one passes away with hands and feet steady, lying on the right side,
without losing control of urine or feces, nor suffering from foul diarrhea or hemorrhaging.
Sixth, at the time of death,
one does not lose right mindfulness, but dies sitting upright rather than lying face down.
Seventh, at the time of death...
Having discoursed on various profound and wondrous teachings, they pass away at the end of their lives.
Eighth, at the time of death,
they aspire to be born in a Buddha-field, and according to that aspiration, they are reborn in the pure lands of the Buddhas.
Born by transformation from a lotus, one constantly beholds all the Buddhas and the assembly of Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas,
never regressing. World-Honored One, if there are sentient beings who deeply delight in this Dharma, you should preach it for them immediately.
There may be those who resolve their minds to seek this Dharma exhaustively, receiving, upholding, reading, and reciting it, and who are likewise not stingy with it,
but extensively analyze and explain it according to the Dharma. Why is this?
A bodhisattva, toward all sentient beings,
constantly gives rise to compassion and wisdom, remaining free from stinginess, parsimony, and envy; thus,
they are able to cultivate and refine the unsurpassed Dharma.
Furthermore, a bodhisattva constantly and diligently cultivates wholesome dharmas for the sake of sentient beings;
therefore, they are truly named a bodhisattva.
What is meant by the term "bodhisattva" (菩提薩埵)?
"Bodhi" signifies wisdom; "Sattva" signifies compassion.
These two terms collectively demonstrate the various meanings of skillful means.
These two dharmas together bear the burden of rescuing sentient beings.
One is then named a Bodhisattva.
World-Honored One, if you would grant me permission,
I shall act for the benefit of all sentient beings, including those with wrong views, nihilistic views, and impaired wisdom.
I now wish, before the Tathāgata,
to proclaim this mantra-samaya of the Amoghapāśahṛdayarāja-dhāraṇī;
I pray that you will graciously accept it.
At that time, the Tathāgata Śākyamuni addressed the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara,
saying: "Good son, you should now speak."
Now is precisely the right time.
The Tathāgata also rejoices that I have empowered you;
do so now for the benefit of all sentient beings in this degenerate age, who are burdened by heavy defilements and possess meager merit.
Furthermore, for the sake of newly initiated bodhisattvas dwelling in the Mahāyāna,
he extensively performs acts of benefit and happiness, carrying out the work of a Buddha.
At that time, the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara...
Having received the Buddha’s permission, he smiled with joyful serenity;
joining his palms in reverence, he gazed up at the Tathāgata without averting his eyes for even a moment and addressed him, saying:
World-Honored One, Tathāgata,
you have now granted me permission to speak this Heart-King Mother Dhāraṇī Mantra Samaya of the Amoghapāśa. As for this samaya:
This is that which all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas together cultivate and purify until they reach the state of liberation;
I now feel compassion for the world.
This divine mantra is taught for the benefit, happiness, and peace of immeasurable sentient beings.

Those who receive and uphold it should first pay homage to the assembly of Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas who practice true and correct compassion; pay homage to the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Golden Light Radiance Roaring Sovereign King; pay homage to the Tathāgata Lion’s Play King; and pay homage to the Tathāgata Immeasurable Light. According to the Sanskrit original, if one recites and upholds [the mantra] in an abbreviated manner, one may omit the prostrations to the Buddhas, Bodhisattvas, and others.
When Maitreya Bodhisattva descends,
he will briefly pay homage to the Tathāgata Amitābha;
[you should likewise proceed] from the Tathāgata Amitābha.
Briefly, having prostrated with reverence to the Triple Gem of the Buddha, Dharma, and Saṅgha, and so forth;
I prostrate to the Tathāgata Maṇiratnarāśirāja, who has gone well; I prostrate to the Tathāgata Samantaprabhāstotraguṇarāśirāja;
I prostrate to the Tathāgata Vairocana.

I pay homage to all such noble beings.
By reciting the secret mantra of the Queen Mother of the Heart-King Amoghapāśa Dhāraṇī of the Noble Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara.
At that time, the Noble Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara immediately entered meditative absorption and carefully contemplated the syllables and phrases of the Mother Dhāraṇī mantra.
All were the color of gold;
their radiance blazed forth, illuminating the worlds of the ten directions.
They arose from samādhi.
Then he spoke the secret mantra of the Mother of the Heart-King Amoghapāśa: *Namaḥ samantabhadraye bhagavati pratyutpannāya namaḥ*.

Oṃ amoghamantralamandale mantrite pāṇḍame mahāpāṇḍame dhuru dhuru svāhā. With this mantra, one consecrates white mustard seeds and water.
By circumambulating the altar and sprinkling [the water],
one establishes the Great Boundary (*mahā-sīmā*), which causes all devas, nāgas, yakṣas, rākṣasas, vināyakas, enemies,
and other such obstacles to be unable to invade, surround, or cause affliction.
Next, the mantra for purifying the five products of the cow is spoken:
Oṃ āmuka parikṣite śuddhaye sāmantena dharidhari śuddhasattva mahāpūjame hūṃ. This mantra consecrates the five pure substances.
One should smear and decorate the interior of the altar.
Or, one may go to any mountain forest, beneath trees, in an araṇya hermitage,
a park, a walking path, a monastery, a town, or a private residence.
In halls, pavilions, beds, couches, places for drawing water, and areas for preparing food— indeed,
in every place where one performs rituals while walking, standing, sitting, or reclining—
one should entirely smear, cleanse, and sprinkle them so that they all become pure.
It can cause all yakṣas, rākṣasas, vināyakas, and malevolent spirits to [be subdued] during times of eating,
times of making offerings, times of recitation,
and times of establishing boundaries.
Whether sitting in meditation, walking in circumambulation, or lying down—
specifically at the time of undressing— no opportunity for harm shall be found;
all devas will provide protection, ensuring they remain free from illness and affliction.
All defilements, obscurations, famines, conflicts, malevolent stars,
calamitous portents, and inauspicious signs shall swiftly be extinguished for the holder of this mantra.
If one can consecrate the five pure substances according to the Dharma,
they may always be used to smear and purify the three pure substances;
these should constantly be consumed by oneself and others.
One will swiftly attain the realization of the secret maṇḍala, mudrā, and samaya of the Amoghapāśahṛdayarāja-dhāraṇī-mantra, appearing before one’s eyes;
furthermore, wherever one goes, there shall be no obstacles whatsoever.
They are constantly praised and revered by kṣatriyas, śramaṇas, brāhmaṇas, householders, and commoners alike.
Furthermore, they constantly see in their dreams palaces and towers made of the seven treasures, as well as flower groves and fruit trees.
One will joyfully behold all virtuous friends and attain purity of body.
Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva shall grant all their aspirations,
and Amitābha Buddha will appear before them in dreams.
If, at the end of life, one is reborn directly in the Western Land of Ultimate Bliss, next recite the mantra for requesting the Dharma, which is:
Oṃ pratame sara sara tiṣṭha tiṣṭha mahā-amoghasamaya svāhā. Recite this seven times within the Dharma altar to address and inform the worthy sages.
"May those who receive the Dharma obtain the samaya.
Next, the mantra for entering the maṇḍala is spoken as follows:
Oṃ vibhūṣaṇālaṃkāra prasara pramiśatu kuru kuru svāhā. This mantra is to be recited each time one enters the maṇḍala.
Then recite [the mantra] twenty-one times.
Enter the maṇḍala, perform the ritual procedures, and present various offerings.
Next, the mantra for scattering flowers is spoken as follows:
Oṃ amuka-anuśāsaya pūjāṃ vāmantrayehi hūṃ. With this mantra, empower the incense and flowers.
Distribute it within the mandala for the one who bestows the dharma.
Next, recite the mantra for combing the hair, which says:
Oṃ āmogha-puṣpa-siddhi dharu dharu tiṣṭha vāgīśvara-mati svāhā. This dhāraṇī is used for consecrating a comb and for binding the hair.
Then, performing the empowerment by placing his hand upon the crown of the recipient's head,
he next spoke the mantra of the jar and the cord, saying:
Oṃ āmukhabhāṣa jalu kṣipa pāri pāri hūṃ. With this mantra, empower the vessel and the cord.
Taking water, one obtains water; then,
having empowered it further,
one may employ it for all purposes as required.
Next, the mantra for the water vessel is spoken as follows:
Oṃ amogha-mi-kāṭa vara-padmāsane jvala-rati kuru kuru hūṃ. This mantra consecrates the jars, vases, and all other vessels.
The center is filled with scented water for its use.
Next, the Consecration Mantra (*abhiṣeka-mantra*) is spoken as follows:
Oṃ (1) bhrūṃ (2) prasare (3) āmukāmi-male (4) vara-vara (5) svāhā (6). This dharma is like a vessel of the seven precious jewels.
Place scented water within it,
empower it once more, and place it inside the mandala to perform the consecration.
Next, the auspicious mantra is further taught as follows:
Oṃ amoghapadme supadme pūṇakare mire mire kāmare svāhā. If one binds the mudrās and the boundary with this mantra:
Burn incense, scatter flowers, hang banners, drive in stakes, kindle fires, and provide food offerings.
Whether holding a rosary, putting on or taking off robes,
or performing any ritual action upon the altar, attend to all such matters.
Furthermore, when reading or reciting the sutras, one should always hold them after consecrating the hands;
for this will be praised by the Buddhas and Bodhisattvas of the ten directions and by all the celestial deities.
Next, the mantra for purifying the mouth is taught as follows:

Oṃ āmukha mimale īvākara smṛtiśuddha pāpaku mala īvasaṃśodhaya dhara dhara sumi marī svāhā. When one wishes to recite, repent, prostrate, or praise the Buddhas and Bodhisattvas, this mantra should be used.
First, empower water with mantras and rinse your mouth and teeth;
thus you shall attain purity.
You will then obtain a tongue-root that is pure, supple, and in color like a lotus.
Next, the mantra for containing incense is proclaimed as follows: "Such is the samaya-mantra;
one should employ excellent white sandalwood, nāgakesara, red lotus, pṛkkā, and saffron."
Take twelve parts each of *kunkuma*, fragrant lotus filaments, the seven substances, and add *karpūra* and *vaca*;
take four parts each of the two remaining quantities, pound them together, and mix with *śarkarā*.
At every time of recitation, empower it and hold it in the mouth.
The breath shall immediately become fragrant and pure, like the scent of the *utpala* flower;
one will constantly be beheld by all Buddhas and Avalokiteśvara, who will joyfully protect and praise them.
For those with ailments such as phlegm, drink-retention, or vomiting, these shall be instantly dissolved and cured.
When the gods of the Heaven of the Thirty-three hear the sound of this dhāraṇī being chanted, they rejoice with reverence and protect sentient beings.
All who hear the voice of such a person shall have their afflictions removed and come to love one another.
Those who constantly maintain the fragrance of the Dharma possess great eloquence and secret spiritual powers.
Hidden at the tip of the tongue, it discerns without obstruction; that which was previously forgotten, it causes one to remember and know.

When the sound of the great syllable *HŪṂ* is uttered, its resonance fills the seven realms, and the hosts of mantra-deities, gods, and celestial immortals immediately arrive within the maṇḍala to provide protection.
Furthermore, with a voice of intense anger, one utters the syllable *bhuḥ*.
With each sound filling the seven realms, the evil Vināyakas and others—ghosts, spirits, demons, and elemental beings—are terrified and flee in all directions.
For those who constantly hold this incense and recite it, all auspicious signs will naturally manifest.
The heavy stains, sins, and darkness are all extinguished; may there never be the interference or harassment of non-human beings.
Next, the mantra for bathing medicine is spoken:
"This samaya-mantra shall be used with nāgapuṣpa, cloves, and cinnamon bark."
Uśīra, tagara, white sandalwood, lotus, keśara, jātī, elā, and white kakkolaka;
Tagara, saffron, pramanda, nakha, and śrīveṣṭaka; Kakkola and clove flowers.
The medicinal herbs ugra and gandhika—taking equal portions of each, pure and refined, combine them and mix with rainwater.
At the time of bathing, empower the mixture and use it to bathe according to the ritual;
thus one will be purified, the skin and body becoming supple, lustrous, and fragrant.
Dispelling calamities and misfortunes, washing away defilements and impurities, one recites and contemplates with purity according to the Dharma.
Whether walking, standing, sitting, or lying down, there shall be no fear or dread.
All evil beings—devas, nāgas, yakṣas, piśācas, and hosts of enemies—will naturally vanish, and one will rejoice without hindrance.
If one constantly bathes with this medicine mixed in warm water, one should know that such a person will swiftly achieve results.
All Buddhas, Bodhisattvas, and celestial deities will look upon them with joy and provide protection, granting supreme vows.
Next, the mantra for eye medicine is spoken as follows:
Regarding this mantra-samaya: take one part each of realgar and ox-gall, thirteen parts each of blue utpala flowers and sea-foam;
having refined these two substances with great care, grind them together and mix with rock honey.
Then, grind them with clear water and employ them after performing the empowerment (adhitiṣṭhanā).
With the application of collyrium, eye-secretions, cataracts, and films are removed;
all Buddhas behold this with joy, and no malevolent ghosts or spirits shall create obstacles. One’s dreams will always be auspicious, and the faculty of the eyes becomes pure.
Next, the mantra for ox-gallstone (*gośīrṣa*) is explained:
In this manner, one should empower the ox-gallstone with the mantra-samaya;
furthermore, using the Mother Dhāraṇī mantra, as well as the mantra of the Furenwang (Krodharāja),
and also the Secret Heart-mantra, one empowers it to apply as a mark upon the forehead while performing the ritual practice.
He immediately causes all evil spirits and ghosts, including the Vināyakas and their like,
to be utterly terrified and flee in fear; just as when birds and beasts see a mass of fire at night,
they are all struck with dread and scatter in haste— except for those who have eliminated the fear of all obstacles.
Whether śramaṇas, brāhmaṇas, or the common people, all who see them will show reverence;
those deities of the dhāraṇīs and mantras dwelling within the maṇḍala will joyfully gaze upon them and increase their protection without weariness,
even when they travel on roads, through wild mountains, or marshy lands.
In all places—by mountain streams, ravines, and gullies—one need not fear the perils of thieves, sorcery, poisons, or evil winds, thunder, lightning, and thunderbolts;
nor the perils of lions, tigers, wolves, and other fierce beasts, nor the calamities of vipers, snakes, and scorpions.
If a practitioner of mantras consecrates this medicine with it, [these dangers shall be averted].
One who binds the mind and must constantly recollect me, and who chants and maintains this *Amogha-mantra*,
I shall come before them and bestow my grace and protection.
Such is the method of the *Amoghapāśahṛdaya-mātṛ-dhāraṇī-mantra*, the bodhicitta-aspiration, and the *samaya*.
Those who protect in this way are the Buddhas; I am also empowered by the truthful words of their compassion.
The power of the heart-mantra of Amoghapāśa, of the dhāraṇī, the secret dharma of the maṇḍala, the mudrās, and samādhi, is further the sincere devotion of the practitioner.
Through the power of my vow to seek awakening, may I cause this person to attain progress and fulfill whatever they desire in their heart.
If there are sentient beings who do not rely on the Dharma but practice flattery and deceit merely for the sake of livelihood, deceiving others and violating the pure conduct; [may I transform them].
Furthermore, if the location is impure, I shall not manifest my presence there;

for what reason could it be otherwise? Because one practices the Dharma in a manner contrary to the Dharma, for this reason, those who uphold the Dharma should sincerely govern their minds in accordance with the Dharma.
The method for cultivating inner and outer purity:
Next, the mantra of the *mālā* (necklace) is proclaimed:
Oṃ amuka-kuśaladhara sarva-pra hūṃ. With this mantra, one consecrates white thread.
One should have a young girl join them together,
like two strands of chopsticks or three strands of thread;
these are the three cords.
Tie the two ends together with a single knot at the center,
reciting the mantra as you do so;
in total, tie three knots.
With both ends joined together,
the mantra-holder should always wear it draped over the shoulder as an ornament.
Next, the mantra for putting on the garment is spoken as follows:
Oṃ amoghapravarana muruḷi jñātikasikasa svādho tṛtara tṛtara svāhā. One should empower the clothing with this mantra and then put it on.
Next, the mantra for removing one’s garments is spoken as follows:
Oṃ amoghasiddhivajra guhyakari bhūmidini pāpame svāhā. This mantra is used when entering or exiting the maṇḍala.
While eating, walking, sitting, or lying down,
one should empower one's hands, remove one's garments, and place them in a clean location;
then, empower them once again.
Next, the mantra for bathing is spoken as follows:
Oṃ bhānuvakra padmāloka varuṇavare abhiṣiñca hūṃ. With this mantra, one consecrates scented water and bathes the body.
Next, the mantra for washing the hands and face is proclaimed as follows:
Oṃ amṛtāloka spharaṇi varṣaṇi julu julu svāhā. With this mantra, one consecrates pure water to wash the hands, wash the face, and rinse the mouth and teeth.
Next, the mantra for protecting the body is spoken as follows:
Oṃ āmukāvaliśani kuru kuru svāhā. With this mantra, one should empower white mustard seeds and water, and sprinkle them upon the body.
No non-human beings will be able to find an opportunity [to harm them].
Protection for others is likewise.
Next, the mantra for bestowing the Dharma is spoken as follows:
Oṃ amoghasamaya mahāpātani tiṣṭha tiṣṭha hūṃ. When one who is being conferred the dharma enters the gate of the maṇḍala, this mantra [is recited].
The Ācārya takes the disciple by the hand, confers empowerment (*adhiṣṭhāna*), and leads him through the entrance of the maṇḍala.
Next, he recites the mantra for protecting his companions, which says:
*Oṃ sarvatrāmogha-vati tiṣṭha rakṣa tu hūṃ*. This mantra is used to empower pure ashes.
If one applies [the substance] to the forehead together with one's disciples,
it will provide protection.
Next, the mantra for rectifying one’s deportment is proclaimed as follows:
Oṃ trile rucye bhadrama amukha hūṃ karmani miri miri svāhā. This mantra, when empowered, is for the ritual performed within the maṇḍala and for making offerings.
Empower yourself and enter the ritual boundary (*maṇḍala*).
Do not further touch or disturb the images of the Buddhas and Bodhisattvas, nor their mantra-seats.
Arrange everything according to the Dharma and perform the various ritual activities.
Next, the mantra of the Jewel Lasso (Ratnapāśa) is proclaimed as follows:
Oṃ ratname mahāratname sara sara samantānāṃ parimṛtyaye āmukhapāśena hulu hulu svāhā. This mantra is used to consecrate a five-colored cord.
The outer boundary of the consecrated altar (maṇḍala) is marked by a fence and gates with banners suspended from them.
Next, the mantra for suspending the banners is taught as follows:
Oṃ miñitrā āmuka vaśitranandana laṅka miśodhaya kṣiṇi kṣiṇi hūṃ. This mantra is to be recited when suspending the banners or when painting them.
One should empower all of them with the mudrā and immediately suspend them;
the paintings should likewise follow this procedure.
Next, the mantra of the arrow is spoken as follows:
Oṃ amoghaśara vajrātuna cara cara svāhā. This mantra is used to empower the arrow.
The same applies to holding a painted arrow.
Next, the mantra for opening the gate of the maṇḍala is taught as follows:
Oṃ vibhūṣāṅga mahā-jvālā-viśuddhe siri siri svāhā. If one who has received the dharma enters the maṇḍala, this mantra [should be recited].
Having completed the consecration of the mandala gate,
he immediately entered the gate of the mandala,
together entering all the wondrous palaces of every buddha-field.
Next, the mantra for purifying the flowers is spoken as follows:
Oṃ nana-mi-citra āmuka puṣpa-parāgata-kiraṇa pūraya vara vara hūṃ. With this mantra, various branches, flowers, and leaves are empowered and inserted into the mouth of the vase.
Furthermore, tie five-colored threads around the neck of the flask,
empower it, and arrange it within the mandala.
Next, the mantra for the incense burner is recited as follows:
Oṃ amoghadhātumimānakhaṭa jvālīścitte ḍambudujvala kheparana samantina jvala svāhā. With this mantra, empower the incense burner and hold it within the maṇḍala.
Offer incense as an offering.
Next, recite the mantra of the precious vase (*ratnaghaṭa*), which is:
Oṃ jvalavati ratnagaṭṭa śalini dhuve dhuve svāhā. This rite empowers the precious vase.
Fill a vessel with ghee, milk, curd,
and rice, arrange it for offering,
and next recite the mantra of the precious vessel as follows:
Oṃ namo bhagavate āmogha-pārame pāraya pāraya hūṃ. This mantra consecrates ceramic vessels.
One should use it for making offerings.
Next, the *argha* mantra is proclaimed as follows:
Oṃ amukā-sapraṇidhāna-nirghātana-vati svāhā. This rite consecrates the *argha*.
One should use it for making offerings.
Next, the mantra of the kamaṇḍalu is spoken:
Oṃ sarani-saraye āmukha-bhojane māta-mātani hūṃ. This is the empowerment of the kamaṇḍalu through this samaya.
With this, one makes offerings.
Next, the mantra for the boundary-positioning is recited as follows:
Oṃ vaṃ-vīrya-vāruṇi amiprajāya-tu samantinaṃ sarvasamavaśaraṇa svāhā. This mantra delineates the boundaries of the altar’s streets and positions.
Consecrate the site of the mandala,
and then demarcate the boundaries and positions of the streets according to the ritual manual,
drawing the design accordingly.
Next, the mantra for painting images is proclaimed as follows:
Oṃ nana-parahaṇa āmuka mudrā jvala jvala svāhā. This rite is performed when painting various images within the maṇḍala and upon the completion of the painting.
One should empower all the various positions in their entirety.
Next, the mantra for the cord-boundary (*sūtrabandhana*) is recited as follows:
*Oṃ āmukhāritana sūtravajri kīli kīli svāhā*. With this mantra, one empowers the five-colored thread.
One should measure all the boundaries of the mandala's perimeter with this thread; likewise,
when one intends to paint an image on a wall, white cotton cloth, or silk,
one should always use this thread mixed with vermilion for the measurement.
The merits [of this practice] are praised by all the noble ones and sages.
Next, the mantra for opening the gates is spoken as follows:
Oṃ vibhūrāje parāṅmukhe amoghapadme hūṃ. When drawing the mandala gate according to this method:
The ground of the empowerment gate is the gateway for drawing the maṇḍala.
Next, the mantra for the golden vessel is proclaimed as follows:
Oṃ nimijña āmogha-karṇa-dhāre kili kili hūṃ. This mantra should be used to empower the golden vessel for the purpose of making offerings.
Next, the mantra for the silver vessel is spoken as follows:
Oṃ tribhuvana-labhyam-iva-bhojani āmukapātre svāhā. This samaya empowers the silver vessel.
One should use it for making offerings.
Next, the mantra for food and drink is proclaimed as follows:
Oṃ mimitā rūpahā rūpā karuṇā jarā jarā amogavati svāhā. With this mantra, one should consecrate various kinds of sweet delicacies, meals, and drinks.
Make abundant offerings.
Next, recite the mantra for floating flowers, which is:
Oṃ jvaṃ khaṃ caṇḍapraline amogharāje dhara dhara svāhā. With this dharma, empower the various flowers and float them upon the water.
Always perform offerings.
Next, the mantra for burning incense is recited as follows:
Oṃ gandhadhūpani samantamigā pīradhūpra hūṃ. This mantra should be recited at every session.
Burn specially consecrated incense as an offering to all Buddhas, Bodhisattvas, Vajras, devas, and others.
Next, the mantra for anointing the altar is taught as follows:
Oṃ amara-kāya-śuddhe amiya-gandha-parapūrṇi pūraya pūraya hūṃ. With this mantra, empower the fragrant mud and scented water.
Mandala Offering. Regarding the *Buddhabhāṣita-Amoghapāśa-Dhāraṇī-Kalpa-Sūtra*, Volume Lower, Zongyì’s record states:
"The *Amoghapāśa-Dhāraṇī-Kalpa* in one work, two fascicles, translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Amoghavajra."
The functions [of this work] are as described in the original sūtra and cannot be fully recorded here;
it consists of thirty-five sheets and is a profound commentary on the *Saṃdhinirmocana-sūtra*.
The *Byōdōbō Jukkan Shō* and other works cite this ritual manual.
As for this manual:
It is the same text as the first and second volumes of the thirty-volume *Amoghapāśa Sūtra* translated by Bodhiruci during the Tang dynasty;
the composition of the prose is also largely identical.
However, regarding the *Mātṛkā-dhāraṇī*,
each sentence has been translated and provided as a footnote;
this is its distinction.
Even a rough grasp of the meaning of the words will yield no small benefit;

alas, they are now missing! What a pity!
